findings.title: Null segment_ids silently skip video deletion for non-javascript platforms
findings.body: When max_segment_id is None, the function returns [] early, skipping deletion of any recordings. This is correct for replays with no segments. But this change also means that if max_segment_id is None but the replay still has orphaned data in storage (e.g., partial write), nothing is cleaned up — not flagged as an error, just silently a no-op. This may be intentional but there's no logging/metric to track how often this happens, making it hard to detect data retention issues.

findings.title: get_environment_info swallows all exceptions broadly
findings.body: The except Exception as e clause catches all exceptions including unexpected ones (e.g., AttributeError due to API misuse), silently absorbing them as 'no environment info' and only logging at info level. This could mask real bugs in production without any alerting, since this is on a non-critical path (comment formatting) but still worth tracking more carefully (e.g. with sentry_sdk.capture_exception) rather than just a logger.info call.

findings.title: GitHub PR comment workflow lost subtitle/culprit information without replacement
findings.body: The old MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE included `subtitle` (culprit) in the per-issue line. The new implementation via get_merged_pr_single_issue_template replaces subtitle with environment info, but these aren't equivalent — culprit information is dropped entirely from the comment body, which is a regression in information shown to developers reviewing the PR comment, unless this was an intentional design decision not stated in the PR description.

findings.title: Detector update() does not persist owner changes atomically with other updates
findings.body: In update(), owner_user_id/owner_team_id are set directly on the instance before instance.save() is called later in the method, but there's no transaction wrapping (unlike create() which wraps everything in transaction.atomic). If an exception occurs after setting the owner fields but before save(), partial state could leak, though in practice this is unlikely since it's all in-memory until save(). More importantly, there's no validation that the new owner (if a team) belongs to the same organization/project, unlike in create() where validate_owner presumably handles this; this inconsistency allows setting an invalid owner during update that would be rejected during create (per test test_owner_not_in_organization only tested for POST not PUT).

findings.title: get_slow_conditions_for_groups called once but still queries potentially large/duplicate dcg_ids
findings.body: The refactor moves get_slow_conditions_for_groups to be computed once in process_delayed_workflows and passed down, which is good for the duplicate call that existed before. However, the function is called with list(event_data.dcg_ids) which may contain duplicate entries if event_data.dcg_ids are not deduplicated; this was pre-existing but worth checking since this is now a single more consequential call feeding both get_condition_query_groups and get_groups_to_fire -- any inconsistency in this shared data now affects both functions instead of being isolated.
